key_insight: A locally compressed method-of-fundamental-solutions preconditioner makes near-contact Stokes simulations stable and efficient by resolving each close pair with a fine local correction while keeping the global solve coarse.
engineering_relevance: This enables accurate, scalable simulation of dense particle suspensions with strong lubrication effects, reducing both GMRES iterations and the number of unknowns per body.
method: Use a two-body preconditioner for each nearly touching disk pair.
Precompute a local fine-grid boundary-value correction for the hard near-contact interaction.
Compress the correction so far-field effects are represented by equivalent coarse sources in the global solve.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a random close packing with φ=0.65, P=10000 disks, and minimum gap 10^-3 solved in 47 GMRES iterations with five digits of accuracy using 72 vector unknowns per body.
watch_item: The approach requires pairwise local precomputations and careful handling of many close interactions, so implementation complexity and memory/precompute costs may grow in very dense or highly nonuniform geometries.
paper_title: Preconditioning for near-contacts in large 2D Stokes flows: a locally compressed method of fundamental solutions
